To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have developed a new approach for vaccination against prion diseases using a recombinant tandem prion protein (tPrP) and CpG-odn as a novel adjuvant that is able to overcome self tolerance and induce CD4 and CD 8 T cell responses in wild type mice.
recombinant tandem PrP and CpG ODN coencapsulated into PLGA microspheres induce specific CD4 and CD 8 T cell responses in wild-type mice and break self-tolerance to prion protein in these animals.

the immunogenicity of recombinantly expressed tandem prion protein (tPrP) was improved by coencapsulating tPrP with CpG-oligodeoxynucleotide in polylactide-co-glycolide microsphere (PLGA- MS) and that this improved immunogenicity was sufficient to induce a specific CD4 and CD 8 T cell response in vivo.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the induction of antiprion immunity in wild-type mice using a combination of tPrP and the adjuvant CpG-ODNs.
the development of a novel vaccine concept for prion diseases, based on the combination of a defined Ag with a potent TLR9 ligand, CpG-ODNs.
the development of an immunotherapeutic approach for the treatment of prion diseases.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the immunogenicity of tPrP is enhanced by the use of CpG-ODNs and PLGA-MS as delivery system.
the use of PLGA-MS as delivery device is an effective strategy to break self-tolerance to PrP in wild-type mice.
tPrP is a promising Ag for vaccination against prion infections, and the combination with CpG-oligodeoxynucleotide and encapsulation into PLGA-MS might be an effective vaccination strategy.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the combination of a recombinant PrP-based immunogen and CpG-OLIGONUCLEOTIDE as adjuvant is able to overcome self-tolerance against prion proteins.
the use of tPrP Ag plus CpG as a vaccine candidate against prion diseases might be a promising approach for prophylactic and/or therapeutic treatment.
tPrP is a promising candidate to overcome self-tolerance to PrP and that CpG-ODNs are a suitable adjuvant for this approach.
The main takeaway from our work is that

we were able to induce a Th1 T cell immune response in wild-type (WT) mice using recombinantly produced dimeric prion protein (tPrP), CpG-oligodeoxynucleotide (ODNs), and polylactide-co-glycolide (PLGA) microspheres.
we have developed a new vaccination strategy for prion disease.

the use of a dimeric prion protein as a vaccine antigen and the coencapsulation of the antigen and CpG-OLGONUCLEOTIDE in biodegradable polymer-based microspheres are promising approaches to induce a T cell response against prion disease.
